officer.body:
Dear Colleague,

Apologies for the cold email. PWLBtoday is fairly new so you may not have come across us yet.

We're built for local authority treasury teams and nothing else: live PWLB rates at both daily fixings, a monthly breakdown of every loan the sector draws, every council's PWLB book priced daily against the DMO's repayment curve, and a training academy for officers and members. There's more — the predictor, the SONIA path, peer metrics, a daily brief — in the brochure at [BROCHURE URL]. We don't sell treasury products, and the data side is free and stays free.

To keep that data and our training relevant we built tools that watch committee papers across every council in the country, so we can see how a council's own figures compare with where the market has gone since. So below are a couple of thoughts on the annual report that went to Cabinet on 25 June, ahead of Full Council on 30 September. You're not being singled out — every authority gets one of these — and there's no agenda in it.

A cross-check first, because it holds cleanly. We hold 10 PWLB loans for Gedling totalling £10,811,577, against the £10.812m at your 2.5.3 and the £10,811,577 in Appendix 1 — to the pound, and the counterparty is the same in every case (all PWLB). The balance sheet closes exactly too: CFR £18,443k less £10,812k of external borrowing less zero other long-term liabilities (your 2.8.3 exempts the leases) is the £7,632k of under-borrowing at 2.2. Prior year closes the same way.

The reason we wrote is the shape of the 25-year-plus bucket. Eight of your ten loans sit in it at a weighted 3.135%, and three of those eight are £1m loans running to 2069, 2071 and 2069 at 1.62%, 1.81% and 2.33% respectively. Those are the cheapest ultra-long PWLB coupons on any borrower's book we've priced — very few councils placed loans in the window when Certainty at fifty years fell below 2%, and none we have read holds three of them together. Nothing in the paper draws attention to them, and we're not suggesting anything should follow; the reading was more "we noticed" than "you should".

On what your book looks like today, we can be exact. Priced against the DMO's premature-repayment curve at yesterday afternoon's fixing (notice 314/26 PM, 14 August 2026), 9 of the 10 loans are below par and the indicative net discount is £3,493,472 — 32.3% of principal. Your 2.5.4 says rescheduling was unviable in the year because of the differential between new-borrowing and premature-repayment rates. That read still holds: today's 50-year Certainty is 6.27% against your sub-2.4% money, and replacing that coupon would cost far more each year than any discount releases. Indicative only — only the DMO can quote — and there is no MRP or accounting treatment behind our number. Your book, priced day by day, is at pwlbtoday.org/loan-analysis.

One standing point, added not for Gedling specifically but because CIPFA's forthcoming Prudential and Treasury Code updates will put it in front of every S151. The liability benchmark — a projection of what a council's external debt would need to be to leave a minimum cash cushion — becomes central. For a council with your shape of book (mostly ultra-long, mostly cheap, and £2.8m of headroom against the original CFR estimate for the year), the pathway that comes out of it is the useful artefact.

On training, three fit the paper. PWLB break costs — mechanics & live calculator covers 2.5.4 and the discount position above. Liability Benchmark: using it in practice picks up the point in the previous paragraph. MRP — policy options and revenue impact goes to your 2.8.a.iv, where the financing-cost ratio moved on MRP timing. All 115 courses are free to local authorities until the end of September at pwlbtoday.org/academy, and free accounts for the whole team.

And if any of it is useful, mentioning it to others would help us more than anything. We're small, word of mouth is most of our marketing, and every sign-up helps us prove the need.

Sign up free → https://pwlbtoday.org/
Follow on LinkedIn → https://www.linkedin.com/company/pwlbtoday/

Russell
https://www.linkedin.com/in/russelltew

Source: Annual Treasury Activity Report 2025/26, Cabinet 25 June 2026, at https://democracy.gedling.gov.uk/documents/s45224/annual-treasury-activity-report-2025-26.pdf, with Appendix 1 at .../s45225/appendix-1-treasury-activity-2025-26.pdf.
